extracted.intended_audience: federal agency administrators and personnel and procurement officers
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance and procedural standards for federal procurement and personnel administration, including organization of procurement divisions, types and roles of personnel offices, civil service classification and appointment sequences, and proposals for decentralizing examinations and grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement Division should be a service unit not a controlling organ
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental consideration ... is that it is a service unit and not a controlling organ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan procurement from the point of view of the operating agency, provide short supply procedures and easily available facilities where needed, avoid encumbering itself and others by trying to do too much. If procurement acts as a service unit it will vindicate the President's hope for greater economy and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan procurement to minimize administrative motions
rubrics_metrics.description: The purchasing mechanism of any organization should be planned to permit operating officials to fill their needs with a minimum of bother and delay, that is to say, with the fewest administrative moves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make actual purchasing transactions as simple as possible so decentralization is practical while maintaining control through budgets, reports, inspection, and clearance of particularly large or specialized orders rather than routing each requisition through a vast centralized process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use predigestion: term contracts, standardized specs, and bid procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The best method which will provide good purchasing with a minimum of administrative motion is that of predigestion: term contracts, and standardized specifications and bid procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By simplifying repetitive procurement decisions in advance (standard specs, term contracts) operating units can make purchases with minimal admin effort while central staff focuses on source development and simplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central procurement authorities should be technicians, not clerks
rubrics_metrics.description: The central procurement authorities of departments and of the Government should be technicians rather than clerks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should develop accessible sources of supply and simplified procedures and educate operating officials in their use, thereby enabling maximum output with minimal administrative effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate personnel offices: service unit vs functional unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel offices fall into two general types. One kind is a 'service unit' which does not usually decide who shall be employed, discharged, or promoted; it acts as an advisory body. The other kind is a 'functional unit' which possesses substantial authority for employment, promotion, and discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service units supply technical counsel and information; functional units can depart from line recommendations and exercise higher authority (subject to top administrator control). Choose structure based on organizational needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose personnel-office type by trade-off between speed and care
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the personnel office is a service or functional unit may depend ... on the relative importance of speed and care in recruitment and promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional offices use objective data requiring time—best where merit and careful selection are priorities. In emergencies or where rapid mass hiring is needed, a service unit acting on operating officials' advice may be preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel offices must provide technical personnel information and administrative functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Both types of offices provide information needed for intelligent personnel actions: measuring and rating employees' abilities, receiving applications and keeping lists of prospective employees, maintaining employee records, processing payrolls, and assisting in problems of personal adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are baseline functions for any personnel office to support operating units and preserve impartiality and institutional welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize interdivisional administrative moves in appointment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of administrative moves in appointment procedures should be minimized to reduce delay and confusion (illustrated by 'Agency A' with only five interdivisional moves versus 'Agency B' with about double and bottlenecks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use direct contacts, simplify required approvals, avoid unnecessary routing (e.g., vague 'political clearance' steps), and prevent putting employees to work long before formal appointment and pay—complex routing increases delay and administrative burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish registers of eligibles arranged by impartial determination of relative merit
rubrics_metrics.description: In operating a civil service system it is necessary to establish registers of eligibles — lists of applicants qualified to fill each type of position, arranged according to an impartial determination of relative merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires dividing examination and application processing among specialized units (e.g., Examination and Application Divisions) and following consistent procedures for compiling and certifying registers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft announcements with skill and exactness to balance openness and selectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The preparation of the announcement is a task demanding skill and exactness since it is necessary 'to make the specifications, such as age and education or experience, sufficiently strict so that too many who are entirely unfit will not apply and at the same time not so strict as to eliminate those who could do the work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare with previous announcements, review language, grade, salary and qualification, consult departments when necessary; improper wording can either flood the register with unfit applicants or exclude qualified ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve secrecy of examination papers
rubrics_metrics.description: It is of course necessary to preserve secrecy so that questions will not be improperly divulged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle preparation, distribution to local boards, and return of papers under secure routines to avoid leaks that would compromise examination integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grade examinations by specialized examiners and appropriate procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are graded by examiners who specialize in the technical field involved. In 'unassembled' examinations the applications, together with supporting papers, theses, etc., are graded in much the same way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualified subject-matter examiners to permit non-mechanical testing where appropriate; ensure grading standards and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification objectives and procedures (twenty-four hour service; groups of three)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Certification Division has as its operating objective 'twenty-four hours service' on requests for eligibles. Eligibles are certified in groups of three; the entire files are sent to the department for selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider availability and need for selective certification; generally only the first three certified may be considered (fourth considered if one declines), and departments typically interview before selecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require medical certificate approval before formal appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate of medical examination by a recognized Federal medical officer must be approved by the Commission before appointment. If appointment is made before approval and the medical certificate is later rejected, the appointment is voided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid voided appointments do not formalize appointments until medical acceptance except in emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct thorough classification investigations for positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should study the classification sheet, familiarize themselves with the organization and functions of the unit, contact classification officers, interview supervisors and the employee (preferably at his desk), observe exhibits of work, and collect comparative material from Commission files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative analysis of similar positions and careful interviews ensure correct allocation of grade and salary; higher-grade positions require review by Chief Examiner and Commissioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralize preparation of specialized examinations while retaining central standards and control
rubrics_metrics.description: Examinations for positions common to many departments should be prepared by the Commission, but those for special positions peculiar to a department could be planned by department personnel officials in accordance with general policies and standards laid down by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A division of work with working agreements would assure specifications suited to departmental needs and reduce delay. The Commission should set standards, require inspections, provide training, and retain authority to demand departmental records and enforce decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge a reasonable fee for civil service applications to reduce frivolous filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Charge a fee for Civil Service Applications; reasonable fees, ranging from $2.00 to $5.00, would limit the volume of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee proceeds could finance Civil Service work. Fees would discourage those not seriously interested or unlikely to qualify; stricter grading of professional exams is a parallel expedient with beneficial effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralize grading of specialized examinations with safeguards for impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The present delay between holding an examination and grading often holds up urgent appointments. Departments that prepare exams could also grade them; examiners in departments presumably have good subject knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguards must insure impartiality: each rater must certify lack of acquaintance with applicants except via official interviews. Department-compiled registers should be reviewable by the Commission and administered by Certification Division like other registers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abolish veterans' preference and apportionment in favor of merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative standing should be determined solely by merit. The apportionment of Washington positions by states and veterans' preference distort merit-based selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Veterans' preference clutters registers with applicants not sufficiently qualified and causes repeated certifications; apportionment can favor geographic origin over qualifications and both practices should be eliminated to ensure meritocracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine decentralized operations with centralized control and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Decentralized operation combined with centralized control would reduce delay while preserving standards. The Commission should keep the function of control, set standards for compiling and grading examinations, enforce them by systematic inspection and spot checks, and have authority comparable to the General Accounting Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure adequate safeguards to prevent favoritism and political manipulation when delegating operational functions; provide training and authority to remove officials guilty of irregularities and to demand departmental records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate decentralization and re-distribution to shorten classification and recruiting procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The volume of Federal personnel work may have grown beyond what can advantageously be handled in full detail by a centralized body. The possibility of shortening classification and recruiting procedures by decentralizing to larger departments is worth investigating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enlarge or redistribute personnel functions where appropriate to achieve reasonable workloads and shorter administrative sequences, but balance against risks to impartiality and standards.
